instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: Hope Keeps Moving
cards.instruction: Turn every disappointment into a new reason the desired outcome is delayed, redirected, or becoming more meaningful.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've turned the calendar page like you. June booked for us, then. We're meant to marry somewhere better than the hall that said no.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I turned it because June's full. Every venue we asked is booked.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, June dealt with. September gives us longer to practise being married.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My parents can't travel in September.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we'll go to them. Ask about their garden; we're finally finding where the wedding belongs.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've put return labels on the books like you. Off to our next shop. This one failed because our readers are somewhere else.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Those go back to the wholesaler. We haven't got money to move shops.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Returns first, then. We'll start with the books we own: one shelf, properly chosen.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can get us a market stall beside the bus stop.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: People waiting with nothing to read. Pack the short stories with me; we've been making customers come too far.

cards.title: Comfort Everyone Else
cards.instruction: Meet every painful moment by comforting someone else more intensely while your own distress becomes harder to hide.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've folded a tissue into a square like you. Nice and composed. Being laid off together doesn't make your day any easier; take the box.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was wrapping my chewing gum. You're wiping your eyes on your sleeve.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep things tidy, then. I'm saving the soft tissues for you. Tell me what worries you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You. Your hands are shaking; you can't pull another tissue out.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Take the whole box. I'll make you tea as soon as I can hold the kettle.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've set out two bowls like you. Double helpings for you; the choir rejecting us doesn't mean you should miss dinner.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I set one for you. You haven't eaten either.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, eating together. So you won't be alone. I'll butter your bread first.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Sit down with me. I don't want you crying in the kitchen.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: All right. Take my bread too; I can't swallow yet, and you should have something warm.

cards.title: Emotional Interest
cards.instruction: Treat comfort, vulnerability, and forgiveness as investments that must eventually be repaid with equal emotional risk.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I put my hand up at lunch like you. My turn for honesty. I told your mother I'm scared she dislikes me; now you owe me a risk.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was reaching for the salt. I didn't ask you to tell her that.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Pass something back, then. I trusted you to risk something too. What scares you about her?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That she'll like you more.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's equal. Tell her on Sunday; mine had an audience, so yours needs one too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've dimmed my lamp like you. Time for confidences. I'll stay through this rejection letter, but you owe me something equally honest.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I dimmed mine for a headache. Do I have to owe you because I'm upset?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Soft light helps. I've stayed through three of these letters with you. Tell me what you're keeping back.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Only if you don't look at me: I stopped applying months ago. This one's old.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Look at me and say it once more. Then we're even, and I'll stay while you decide what to do next.

cards.title: Ready on My Terms
cards.instruction: Agree to be honest, hopeful, or vulnerable only in forms that preserve your emotional safety.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've set a timer like you. One-question conversations; sensible. I'll discuss last night's rent argument, not the whole year.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mine's for the oven. The whole year matters; you've been pulling away.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep the timer running. Ask one question, and let me finish before you answer.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Were you going to move out?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I packed a bag. It's still upstairs. Please let that be the whole answer until the timer goes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've moved my chair beside yours by the door. Easy exits. I'll talk about trying again from here.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I moved away from the radiator. Are you planning to run?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Cooler here, then. Knowing I can go is helping me stay.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We can stop whenever you need to.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I want to come home. But don't hand me a key yet; saying it is enough for tonight.

cards.title: The Same Ending
cards.instruction: Use every new emotional detail as evidence that the same feared ending is becoming inevitable.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've copied 'Regards' from your message. No kisses; a proper goodbye.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's my work-email signature. I was sending you a soup recipe for your cold.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Businesslike, yes. That's how my last breakup started: polite advice instead of 'love you'.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll bring you soup tonight.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The final kindness. Will it be in a container you don't need back?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've crossed out our lunches like you. A clean calendar. First this, then fewer calls, then you ask for the key.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I crossed out today. I'm exhausted; I haven't cancelled every lunch.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, today first. That's what he said before seeing me became another job.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Tomorrow, then. I'll book our usual restaurant.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: He chose a restaurant too. Public enough that I couldn't beg. Book the corner, please.
